ctx.x: Yeah, Bill Robinson. And a big bale of cottons on the stage, right in the center stage. And she's in this bale of cottons. And when we start to play, that bale of cottons just open up like that. And she come out. And she's there. Oh, she could go. Oh, they had us on. We had beautiful cover halls, you know, different colors.
Is that the one that had the steamboat? Yeah, it's better. Is Lawrence Dewey the... Lawrence Dewey was the carnet band. Yeah, I've seen that picture.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: You know how Boa Jingles used to dance with wooden shoes on. She had the same thing.

ctx.x: No. Mabel Elaine and her jazz band. She's a white girl. She used to clunk band. You know how Boa Jingles used to dance with wooden shoes on. She had the same thing. She used to be in a bale of cotton. She was blackface. When you get on the stage, that bale of cotton was out there. They couldn't go out. We'd be all lying around in this cotton, see, with a couple of holes on, satin cover holes, different colors, and bandana, hangers, and hats. So I had, when we started playing, this fave of cotton opened up. And…
